75421-1: This is Darth Vader's own fighter, the TIE Advanced, from the thrilling end of A New Hope (1977). As the Rebels dive into the Death Star's trench, Vader hunts them down one by one, until Han Solo swoops in out of nowhere and blasts him into a spin, sending Vader tumbling off into space. The Rebel Fleet Trooper comes from the very first scene of the film, when Vader's stormtroopers storm Princess Leia's ship and the troopers valiantly try to hold them off.
75423-1: "Red Five, standing by." Red Five was Luke Skywalker's call sign in the attack on the first Death Star. With R2-D2 in the droid socket behind him, Luke races down the trench, switches off his targeting computer, trusts the Force, and fires two torpedoes into an exhaust port barely two metres wide. Boom: the most famous shot in film history. Princess Leia waits back at the Rebel base, watching on the screen.
75427-1: The climax of Return of the Jedi (1983). In his throne room high in the second Death Star, the Emperor tries to tempt Luke to the dark side. Luke duels his own father, Darth Vader, and refuses to give in. When the Emperor attacks Luke with Force lightning, Vader finally turns against his master to save his son: one of the greatest moments of redemption in any story. Outside, speedy Rebel A-wings dart through the giant space battle.
75426-1: Han Solo calls the Millennium Falcon "the fastest hunk of junk in the galaxy". It made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs, and Han won it from his friend Lando in a game of cards. In A New Hope, Obi-Wan and Luke hire Han and Chewbacca to fly them to Alderaan. On the way, R2-D2 and Chewie play holochess (Chewie hates losing), while Luke practises with his lightsaber against a floating training remote.
75425-1: "You will never find a more wretched hive of scum and villainy," warns Obi-Wan as he and Luke arrive in Mos Eisley, a notorious spaceport on Tatooine. Inside the cantina, the band plays the same jaunty tune over and over, aliens of every shape lurk in the shadows, and Han Solo has a tense meeting with Greedo, a bounty hunter who wants the money Han owes to Jabba the Hutt. It's where Luke first meets Han and Chewie.
75424-1: On the forest moon of Endor, in Return of the Jedi, the mighty Empire is beaten by teddy bears. Well, sort of. Small, furry Ewoks like Wicket ambush the Imperial army with logs, rocks, nets and catapults, toppling two-legged AT-ST walkers, which fans call "chicken walkers". The Ewoks even pinch an Imperial speeder bike. It's a story about how the small and clever can defeat the big and powerful.
75420-1: Before he was a hero, Luke Skywalker was a bored farm boy on the desert planet Tatooine, zooming around in his battered X-34 landspeeder. In A New Hope, Jawas sell his uncle two droids, Luke drinks blue milk at the family table, and later, at a checkpoint in Mos Eisley, Obi-Wan waves his hand and tells the stormtroopers "These aren't the droids you're looking for." It's a Jedi mind trick, and it works. The boxy Gonk droid is a walking battery, and it really does say "gonk".
75422-1: In The Empire Strikes Back (1980), Luke crash-lands his X-wing in a steamy swamp on Dagobah to find the great Jedi Master Yoda. At first, Yoda pretends to be a silly little creature rummaging through Luke's things. Then the training begins: Luke runs through the jungle with Yoda on his back, does handstands, and learns that "size matters not" when Yoda lifts the whole X-wing out of the swamp with the Force. "Do. Or do not. There is no try."
30728-1: The Razor Crest is the battered old gunship that the Mandalorian lives in, sleeps in and keeps his prisoners in (frozen in carbonite in the back). It's where he first takes care of Grogu, and it gets patched up, shot at and stripped for parts again and again in the TV show. In season two, it's blasted to pieces from space. That's why fans were so excited to see it back in LEGO's movie range.
75436-1: At the start of The Mandalorian season two, Mando borrows a speeder bike from Peli Motto, a mechanic in Mos Eisley, and roars across the dunes of Tatooine searching for another Mandalorian. With Grogu tucked into a satchel on the side, the pair look like a dad and toddler on a very fast bicycle. What they find instead is a town marshal wearing some very famous armour (see Cobb Vanth's Speeder).
75443-1: This little set lets younger builders imagine Grogu's everyday adventures: snacks, critters and a catapult. In the TV show, Grogu is fifty years old but still a baby, because his species grows up very slowly. He loves a snack, and his favourite mischief is grabbing food he isn't supposed to eat, including a whole egg collection that belonged to a frog lady.
75410-1: The N-1 Starfighter first flew in The Phantom Menace (1999), when nine-year-old Anakin Skywalker flew one by accident and destroyed a droid control ship. Decades later, in The Book of Boba Fett, mechanic Peli Motto rebuilds an old N-1 as a hot rod for Mando. Fun fact: R5-D4, the little red droid in this set, is the same droid the Jawas tried to sell Luke's uncle in A New Hope, until his "bad motivator" popped.
75437-1: Cobb Vanth is the marshal of a tiny desert town on Tatooine, and he's wearing Boba Fett's actual armour, which he bought from Jawas. His speeder is just as cool: it's built from the engine of a podracer, and fans think it was young Anakin's very own podracer from The Phantom Menace. Cad Bane is a blue-skinned bounty hunter with a wide-brimmed hat who started in the Clone Wars cartoon and later came to Tatooine to face Cobb in a showdown in The Book of Boba Fett.
75444-1: AT-RTs are small, open two-legged walkers, first ridden by clone scouts in The Clone Wars and Revenge of the Sith. Years after the Empire fell, its leftover forces, the Imperial Remnant, are still out there, using old machines like these. In The Mandalorian and Grogu they're among the enemies Mando faces, and the defence tower here gives him something to storm.
75451-1: Embo is a Kyuzo bounty hunter from The Clone Wars cartoon, famous for his wide metal hat, which he can throw like a frisbee and use as a shield. He's never far from his Anooba, a fierce, loyal hunting beast. Here he and his pet Keibu turn up at a palace of the Hutts, the gangster family of Jabba the Hutt, alongside Mando, Grogu and a towering sentry droid.
75460-1: After the Rebels won the war, they became the New Republic, and their pilots kept flying upgraded X-wings like this one, with blue stripes instead of red. Carson Teva is a New Republic pilot who first appeared in The Mandalorian season two, patrolling the Outer Rim and keeping an eye on trouble. Colonel Ward is a New Republic officer introduced in The Mandalorian and Grogu.
75445-1: Anzellans are tiny aliens, about the size of your hand, and they're the best droidsmiths in the galaxy. The most famous one is Babu Frik from The Rise of Skywalker, who squeaks "Hey hey!" while fixing C-3PO. Because they're so small, LEGO made special mini figures for them instead of normal minifigures. Their starship is built for crews that would fit in your pencil case.
75447-1: The Razor Crest is Mando's home, his office and his getaway car all in one: a battered old gunship with a cockpit in front, a carbonite freezer in the back for frozen prisoners, and a bunk where Mando sleeps. This new version is part of LEGO's movie range, with Colonel Ward and Zeb Orrelios, a big purple Lasat warrior from the cartoon Star Wars Rebels.
75454-1: AT-ATs are the giant four-legged Imperial walkers that stomped across the ice planet Hoth in The Empire Strikes Back: intimidating, slow and almost unstoppable. Long after the Empire's defeat, the Imperial Remnant still has a few. In the movie range they come with a new kind of snowtrooper, Commander Barro, and a small starfighter called the INT-4. Expect stomping. Lots of stomping.
75459-1: The Lambda-class shuttle is the elegant Imperial transport with three wings that fold up like a bird landing. In Return of the Jedi, Han, Leia and Chewie steal one, called Tydirium, and sneak past the Empire using an old secret code. This set's shuttle carries two villains from The Mandalorian: Moff Gideon, who wields the black-bladed Darksaber, and Dr Pershing, the nervous scientist who wanted to study Grogu.
75453-1: This set comes from the second ever episode of The Mandalorian, "The Child". Jawas strip Mando's ship for parts and carry them off in their enormous, rusty Sandcrawler. To get the parts back, Mando must fetch a Mudhorn egg, and the Mudhorn, a huge horned beast, charges him again and again. Just when it's about to finish him, little Grogu raises his hand and lifts the monster into the air with the Force. It was the first time we saw what the Child could do.
75403-1: When Grogu first appeared in The Mandalorian in 2019, nobody knew his name. Fans called him "Baby Yoda" and he became an internet sensation overnight. He travels in a floating pram, like a little egg-shaped hovercraft, and in season two he famously sneaks blue macaron biscuits from a classroom while nobody's looking.
75446-1: In The Mandalorian, Mando takes Grogu in as a foundling, a child adopted into the Mandalorian creed. Later, Mando has a tiny chainmail shirt forged for him out of beskar, the super-strong Mandalorian metal. By season three, Grogu is officially Mando's apprentice, and in the film he wears beskar armour of his own. Little, green and armoured: a fearsome combination.
40856-1: BrickHeadz are LEGO's square-headed, big-eyed figures, built from about a hundred pieces each. This pack turns the heroes and villains of The Mandalorian and Grogu into cuties: Mando, Grogu, Colonel Ward, a tiny Anzellan droidsmith and an Imperial Remnant Snowtrooper.
75448-1: The Clone Shock Troopers wear red-marked armour and guard the capital planet, Coruscant, so they're sometimes called the Coruscant Guard. In the Clone Wars they're the Republic's police and palace guards. LEGO imagined them climbing into a giant battle mech, which never happens on screen but is much more fun.
75400-1: Plo Koon is a wise Jedi Master from the planet Dorin. He wears a mask and goggles because he can't breathe air with so much oxygen in it. In The Clone Wars cartoon he's a kind, fatherly hero, the Jedi who found little Ahsoka Tano and brought her to the Jedi Temple. His starfighter is a sleek Delta-7, and he flies it with clone pilots he calls his "Wolfpack".
75411-1: Darth Maul is the red-and-black Sith with horns and a double-bladed lightsaber who duels Obi-Wan and Qui-Gon in The Phantom Menace (1999). At the end of that film he's cut in half and falls down a shaft, and everybody thought he was gone. But in The Clone Wars he comes back with robotic spider legs, full of rage and revenge. A mech seems perfect for a villain who's already half machine.
75449-1: In the final story of The Clone Wars, Ahsoka Tano leads a battalion of clones, the 332nd, to free the planet Mandalore from Darth Maul. The clones paint orange markings on their helmets in honour of Ahsoka. On the other side are Maul's Super Commandos: Mandalorian warriors in red and black armour with jetpacks. It's one of the most exciting battles in the whole cartoon.
75412-1: In the TV series Ahsoka (2023), the Night Troopers are stormtroopers who've served the evil Grand Admiral Thrawn for years on a distant, mysterious planet, and their cracked, painted armour gives them a ghostly, ancient look. Death Troopers, in all-black armour, are the Empire's elite bodyguards, first seen in Rogue One. Both sides of this pack are bad guys, so you'll need some heroes to fight them.
75372-1: The Clone Wars began with armies of identical clones fighting armies of droids that say "Roger, roger". The Battle of Christophsis, in the 2008 Clone Wars film, was one of the first big battles, with clones defending against wave after wave of droids. Super Battle Droids are the bulky, tougher ones with blasters built into their arms, and the Tri-Droid is a creepy three-legged robot that clambers over rubble.
75431-1: The 327th Star Corps are clones with yellow markings, led by Jedi Master Aayla Secura and her clone commander, Bly. They fight on Felucia, a planet covered in giant, glowing fungus and enormous plants. The AT-RT is their quick scout walker, and the Dwarf Spider Droid is a nasty little four-legged robot with a cannon for a face.
75432-1: The V-19 Torrent is a small Republic fighter from the early Clone Wars, with three wings that fold up for landing. Obi-Wan Kenobi was often in the thick of the action in The Clone Wars cartoon, and so was Asajj Ventress, a fierce assassin who worked for the evil Count Dooku and fought with two curved red lightsabers. Later, she quit the dark side and became a bounty hunter: a classic antihero.
75402-1: The ARC-170 is a big three-seat Republic fighter, from the spectacular opening battle of Revenge of the Sith (2005), high above the city-planet Coruscant. Clone pilot Odd Ball flies alongside Obi-Wan and Anakin as they race to rescue the kidnapped Chancellor. The ARC-170 has a pilot, a co-pilot, a tail gunner and an astromech droid, here R4-P44.
75435-1: The MTT (Multi-Troop Transport) first appeared in The Phantom Menace, invading the peaceful planet Naboo. It's basically a giant armoured bus for robots: a rack slides out of the front and unfolds, and over a hundred Battle Droids march out. In this set it's on Felucia, facing Aayla Secura and Commander Bly.
75413-1: The Clone Turbo Tank, which LEGO calls the Republic Juggernaut, is a ten-wheeled monster from Revenge of the Sith. The set's minifigures come from a battle on the frozen, crystal-covered planet Mygeeto, where Jedi Master Ki-Adi-Mundi (the one with the tall, cone-shaped head) leads Commander Bacara and the Galactic Marines into battle.
30727-1: Darth Vader's TIE Advanced has curved wings and a fancier design than an ordinary TIE Fighter, because only the best for the Dark Lord of the Sith. It's the ship he flies in the Death Star trench, in the last thrilling minutes of A New Hope.
75414-1: LEGO Star Wars: Rebuild the Galaxy (2024) is a cartoon where a nobody called Sig Greebling stumbles on a mysterious secret and accidentally jumbles the whole Star Wars galaxy. Suddenly Darth Vader is a Jedi, Jar Jar Binks is a Sith Lord, and familiar vehicles get wild new paint jobs. The Force Burner is a hot-rod version of the Snowspeeders from The Empire Strikes Back, the ones Rebel pilots flew around the legs of giant walkers on Hoth.
75399-1: The U-wing is the Rebel Alliance's troop carrier, from Rogue One (2016) and the TV series Andor. Cassian Andor is a Rebel spy who flies it, and K-2SO is his reprogrammed Imperial droid, who says exactly what he thinks, usually that their chances of survival are terrible. Dedra Meero is the ruthless Imperial officer hunting the Rebels in Andor. In Rogue One, a U-wing carries the heroes on the mission to steal the Death Star plans, the plans that let Luke blow it up.
75433-1: In Attack of the Clones (2002), Obi-Wan tracks a mystery to Kamino, a planet of endless ocean and rainstorms, where the tall, polite Kaminoans like Lama Su are secretly building an army of clones. Every single clone is copied from one man: the bounty hunter Jango Fett. His young "son", Boba, is an exact clone too. Then comes an epic chase through an asteroid field, where Jango drops seismic charges, bombs that go silent and then BWOOOM.
75394-1: The very first shot of the first Star Wars film (1977) is an Imperial Star Destroyer, rumbling overhead for what seems like forever as it chases Princess Leia's little ship. Star Destroyers are wedge-shaped warships about 1.6 kilometres long, the symbol of the Empire's power. Cal Kestis, the young Jedi in this set, is the hero of the Star Wars Jedi video games.
75389-1: Another Rebuild the Galaxy set. In the jumbled-up galaxy of the cartoon, even Han Solo's famous Millennium Falcon has gone over to the dark side, turned black and red with a menacing mini superlaser. The minifigures are remixes too: Darth Jar Jar, Jedi Vader, Darth Rey and Beach Luke (yes, Luke in beach clothes).
40795-1: The orange flight suit is what Luke wears on his most famous day: the attack on the Death Star in A New Hope, flying as Red Five. Just a farm boy a few days earlier, and now a hero of the Rebellion.
75438-1: Yoda is about 900 years old, only 66 centimetres tall, and the greatest Jedi Master of all. He talks backwards ("Judge me by my size, do you?") and trained Jedi for 800 years. In Attack of the Clones, the tiny, wobbly old Jedi suddenly whirls into an acrobatic lightsaber duel with Count Dooku, and cinema audiences cheered.
75439-1: Darth Vader is probably the most famous villain in cinema: the black helmet, the cape, the terrifying breathing. Once he was Anakin Skywalker, a Jedi hero, until he was seduced by the dark side. In The Empire Strikes Back, he tells Luke the truth in one of the biggest plot twists ever: "No, I am your father."
75452-1: BB-8 is the rolling droid from The Force Awakens (2015), carrying a secret map to find the missing Luke Skywalker. His round body rolls along while his head stays balanced on top (in the films, real working BB-8 robots were built for many scenes). He's brave, loyal and expressive, and at one point he gives Finn a "thumbs up" using a little lighter.
75434-1: K-2SO is an Imperial security droid that the Rebel spy Cassian Andor reprogrammed to be on his side. The trouble is, it also removed his filter, so K-2SO says exactly what he thinks: blunt, sarcastic and very funny. In Rogue One (2016) he tells everyone their chances of success are dreadful, then helps them anyway, heroically.
75379-1: R2-D2 has been in every main Star Wars film. In A New Hope he carries Princess Leia's secret message ("Help me, Obi-Wan Kenobi. You're my only hope"), and he's always rescuing people with a hidden tool or a well-timed beep. His third leg drops down when he needs to roll over rough ground. Darth Malak comes from Knights of the Old Republic, a 2003 video game set thousands of years before the films.
75416-1: Chopper is the grumpiest droid in the galaxy. In the cartoon Star Wars Rebels (2014 to 2018), he's part of the crew of the Ghost, a Rebel ship flown by Hera Syndulla. He zaps people, plays pranks, mutters rude things in beeps and somehow always saves the day. He turned up again in the live-action series Ahsoka in 2023, as cranky as ever.
75461-1: The Darth Vader minifigure has been a LEGO favourite for more than 25 years. This set builds him at six times the normal size, with the same blocky hands, round head shape and moving arms and legs. It's an homage to the little figure, rather than to the film.
75430-1: Wicket W. Warrick is the first Ewok we meet in Return of the Jedi. He finds Princess Leia in the forest after she falls from a speeder bike, and after poking her with his spear and being offered a snack, he decides she's a friend. He leads her to his village, where the Ewoks think C-3PO is a god, and later helps the Rebels win the Battle of Endor.
75428-1: The Battle Droids of The Phantom Menace (1999) are skinny, clattering robots who answer every order with "Roger, roger". The STAP (Single Trooper Aerial Platform) is a tiny flying scooter they ride while chasing Qui-Gon Jinn and Jar Jar Binks through the forests of Naboo. Standing on one is about as safe as it looks.
75398-1: C-3PO is a protocol droid, "fluent in over six million forms of communication", and very, very anxious. Here's the amazing bit: he was built from spare parts by young Anakin Skywalker on Tatooine, as told in The Phantom Menace. So Darth Vader built C-3PO. Threepio spends most of the films worrying, complaining and calculating the odds of disaster.
75455-1: Boba Fett barely speaks in The Empire Strikes Back (1980), but his cool armour made him a legend. He tracks the Millennium Falcon to Cloud City and carries Han Solo away, frozen in carbonite, to Jabba the Hutt. In Return of the Jedi he falls into the Sarlacc pit and everyone thought he was gone, until he climbed out decades later in The Mandalorian. He has his own series, The Book of Boba Fett.
75328-1: Din Djarin, the Mandalorian, follows a strict creed: never take your helmet off in front of anyone. His helmet is made of beskar, a Mandalorian metal so strong it can stop a lightsaber. "This is the way," say the Mandalorians, and the phrase became a famous catchphrase.
75408-1: Jango Fett was the deadliest bounty hunter of his time, so the Kaminoans chose him as the template for the whole clone army in Attack of the Clones. That's why the clone troopers' helmets look so much like his: the T-shaped visor came first. The little antenna on the side is a rangefinder for targeting.
75415-1: Kylo Ren is the dark warrior of the Sequel Trilogy (2015 to 2019). Under the helmet he's Ben Solo, the son of Han Solo and Princess Leia, and the grandson of Darth Vader, which is why he wears a dark mask in Vader's style. It even changes his voice. His crackling, cross-shaped red lightsaber is just as famous.
75429-1: AT-AT drivers sit in the head of the giant walkers that attack the Rebel base on Hoth in The Empire Strikes Back. Their helmets are a cousin of the TIE pilot helmet, with breathing tubes and red Imperial symbols. The lead walker, commanded by General Veers, destroys the shield generator and lets the Empire win the battle.
75458-1: This helmet is worn by Imperial Remnant AT-RT drivers in the 2026 film The Mandalorian and Grogu. Its design is very similar to the Shoretroopers from Rogue One, the beach-guarding stormtroopers of the tropical planet Scarif.
75375-1: The Millennium Falcon is probably the most famous spaceship in film history. Han Solo won it from Lando Calrissian in a game of cards, and its shape was supposedly inspired by a hamburger with an olive on the side. It's been in seven of the nine main Star Wars films.
75406-1: Kylo Ren's command shuttle, from The Force Awakens and The Last Jedi, looks like a giant black bat. Its huge wings fold up when it lands, and stretch out tall when it flies, making it look even more sinister.
75440-1: The Battle of Hoth, in The Empire Strikes Back, starts with the Empire's giant AT-AT walkers marching across the snow. Blasters bounce off their armour, so the Rebels try something daring: Snowspeeder pilots fire a harpoon and tow cable, fly round and round the walker's legs, and trip it up. Down it crashes. It's one of the most brilliant tactics in Star Wars.
75441-1: Venators are the Republic's red-striped Star Destroyers, seen in Revenge of the Sith and all through The Clone Wars cartoon. Anakin Skywalker's own Venator was called the Resolute. They carry starfighters in a hangar running the length of the ship. The Invisible Hand, which this set matches in scale, is the villain General Grievous's flagship.
75407-1: "A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away...." Then, BLAM: the huge yellow Star Wars logo appears with a crash of music and flies off into space, followed by the famous scrolling words. That opening has started almost every Star Wars film since 1977, and this logo is its most famous moment.
75417-1: AT-STs, the two-legged "chicken walkers", patrol the forests of Endor in Return of the Jedi. They look terrifying, but the Ewoks beat them with logs and rocks, and Chewbacca hijacks one, roaring with delight as he drives it into battle against its own side.
75382-1: TIE Interceptors are faster, sharper and more dangerous than ordinary TIE Fighters, with pointed wings split into a dagger shape. They swarm through the space battle above Endor in Return of the Jedi, chasing the Millennium Falcon and the Rebel fleet.
75442-1: In The Book of Boba Fett, Peli Motto rebuilds a battered old N-1 Starfighter for Mando, after the Razor Crest is destroyed. She strips off the yellow paint, souped up the engines and gives it a droid socket where Grogu can ride. Mando is delighted. The N-1 originally comes from Naboo, in The Phantom Menace.
75409-1: Jango Fett's ship (the Slave I) is shaped like an upright oval, flying tilted on its side. In Attack of the Clones, Jango and young Boba flee Kamino with Obi-Wan in pursuit and lead him into an asteroid field, where seismic charges go off in eerie silence followed by a gigantic BWOOOM. The sound effect is one of the most famous in Star Wars.
75397-1: Jabba the Hutt's sail barge, from Return of the Jedi, floats over the Tatooine desert to the Sarlacc pit, where Jabba plans to feed Luke, Han and Chewbacca to a monster with tentacles and a beak. But R2-D2 is hiding a surprise: Luke's lightsaber. Luke flips into the air, catches it, and the heroes fight their way out, while Leia defeats Jabba and the whole barge blows up.
75367-1: The UCS Venator is a giant version of the Republic warships from Revenge of the Sith and The Clone Wars, with Captain Rex, Anakin's loyal clone captain, and Admiral Yularen, who commands Anakin's ship, the Resolute. In the opening of Revenge of the Sith, whole fleets of Venators fight above Coruscant in one of the biggest space battles in the saga.
75457-1: The Executor is Darth Vader's personal flagship, a Super Star Destroyer about 19 kilometres long, more than ten times the length of a normal Star Destroyer. In The Empire Strikes Back, Vader calls a gang of bounty hunters to its bridge (Boba Fett, Bossk, IG-88, Dengar, 4-LOM and Zuckuss) and offers a reward for finding the Millennium Falcon. At the end of Return of the Jedi, a single damaged A-wing crashes into its bridge, and the colossal ship plunges into the Death Star.
75192-1: This set has two crews because the Falcon has two lives. In the original trilogy, it's Han Solo's beloved smuggling ship. Then, more than thirty years later in The Force Awakens, Rey and Finn steal "the garbage" to escape from the desert planet Jakku, and it turns out to be the Falcon. When Han and Chewbacca find it again, Han smiles and says the line fans had waited decades to hear: "Chewie, we're home."
75419-1: "That's no moon. It's a space station." The Death Star is the Empire's moon-sized battle station, powerful enough to destroy a whole planet with its superlaser. In Rogue One, we learn that its designer, Galen Erso, secretly built in a tiny weakness, a thermal exhaust port. The Rebels steal the plans, and in A New Hope Luke fires the shot that blows it to smithereens. This set packs in scenes from both films.
75456-1: This year's Advent Calendar is full of tiny creatures from the Star Wars galaxy, such as the shaggy banthas of Tatooine and the blurrgs of The Mandalorian, lumpy, grumpy beasts that Kuiil teaches Mando to ride (after Mando falls off quite a lot).
40806-1: The real AT-AT walkers first stomped across the snows of Hoth in The Empire Strikes Back (1980). This one has swapped its armour for gingerbread and icing. It isn't from any film. It's pure festive imagination, a mash-up of Star Wars and Christmas baking.
